status: Development Helm wiring, real API trust bootstrap, and scoped permissions verified locally; durable delivery remains disabled by default pending installed acceptance and retention

environment.API: Kubernetes 1.37.0 kube-apiserver and etcd for RBAC, trust bootstrap, Service/NetworkPolicy validation, and admission; fake clients in unit tests

checks.command: KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS=<Kubernetes 1.37.0 darwin/arm64 assets> PTAH_REQUIRE_ENVTEST=1 GOFLAGS=-p=1 go test -count=1 -json ./test/envtest/webhook -run TestResult
GOCACHE=<shared Go cache> GOFLAGS=-p=1 make fmt-check vet verify-runner-protocol e2e-static
checks.note: The static gate executes both render-dependent tests skipped by the ordinary race invocation, supplying PTAH_ADMISSION_RENDER and PTAH_PRIVILEGE_RENDER. The gate covers existing default/external-certificate and namespace layouts; new enabled-mode RBAC also has dedicated render and real API tests.

proved: The enabled Helm path wires the receiver Service, six-file read-only trust projection, manager flags, and independent result rotator flags. It precreates the projection/journal Secrets, public enrollment ConfigMap, and separate Lease. Incompatible external webhook trust or a conflicting webhook port is refused.

Enabled manager permissions are GET/CREATE on result records and CREATE on Secrets, with no Secret read/update or pods/log grant. Rotator permissions name only the installation Secrets, policy, and Leases. The real API server evaluates these rendered grants for separate manager and rotator identities.

The controller-write webhook now routes every manager Secret request. A real API test refuses arbitrary manager Secret creation despite its CREATE grant; canonical delivery credentials remain admitted, and unrelated administrator Secrets remain outside the guard.

With actual rendered RBAC and precreated objects installed into envtest, the result rotator persists its bootstrap journal, restarts from it, and writes the enrollment policy and six trust files. An absent endpoint refuses rotation readiness. The receiver accepts the explicitly copied projection, while manager API Secret GET remains Forbidden.

The optional ingress policy requires explicit infrastructure peers for webhook, health, and metrics. Receiver ingress is restricted to operation Pods of both families and this release rotator. The real API accepts the rendered Service and NetworkPolicy. All nine durable Job builders are covered by the receiver egress example, with the exact receiver destination and port.
notProved: The development option is disabled by default. Default installed Jobs still use logs, and the 64 MiB workaround remains until full default-logging acceptance. This is not the completed transport rollout.

Envtest runs no Deployment, kubelet, CNI, SQL process, or manager reconciliation. Explicit disk projection does not prove kubelet Secret refresh; API acceptance does not prove NetworkPolicy enforcement. Admission handlers still use administrator reads in their separate fixture.
Full Job-to-controller delivery, the maximum supported Plan, log removal, manager replacement, loss after SQL mutation, HA, installed CA rotation, and measured Lease/progress contention.
Retention and authorized deletion, garbage collection, quota, backup/restore, metrics, the supported Kubernetes/engine matrix, and full make verify on this commit.
Issue 586 end-to-end DoDs and issue 242 closure remain open. No tag, release, or merge was performed.
